modules.module_title: MSME/AET/01 Embedded Program Development on different microcontroller

pcs.pc_description: • Explain the difference between a high-level programming • language and a low-level programming language
• What are the key features and characteristics of the C • programming language.
• What are decision-making statements in C, and why are they • important in programming.
• Differentiate between the if statement, the else-if statement, • and the switch statement in C
• Provide an example of a C program that uses a conditional • statement to determine if a number is even or odd
• Create a C program that uses a structure to represent a • student's information and a pointer to manipulate that • information.
• Explain the concept of pointers in C. How are they different • from regular variables
• Write a C program that calculates the average of an array of • numbers using a user-defined function.
• What is an array in C, and how does it differ from a regular • variable? Provide an example.
• What are peripherals in the context of microcontrollers and • embedded systems, and why are they essential.
• Write a simple Embedded C program that blinks an LED • connected to a PIC microcontroller. Explain the code logic.
• Configure and use a timer in a PIC microcontroller using • Embedded C code
• Write an Embedded C program that generates PWM signals to • control the brightness of an LED using a PIC microcontroller
• Provide an example of using a counter to count external events • or pulses in a PIC microcontroller
• The key features and specifications of the LPC2148 • microcontroller, including its architecture and clock frequency.
Describe the characteristics of the ADC, DAC in LPC2148 including resolution and voltage output range
• Functioning of the UART/SPI/I2C communication protocols of • the LPC2148 microcontroller.
Introduction to Cortex-M3 series
• Some common use cases or applications where the LPC1768 • microcontroller (Cortex-M3 series) is typically deployed
• The architecture of the Cortex-M3 core, focusing on its key • components, such as the pipeline, registers, and execution • modes.
• Examples of common peripherals that can be interfaced with • the LPC1768, such as sensors, displays, and communication • modules
• What is a real-time operating system (RTOS), and how does it • differ from conventional operating systems
• Describe the concept of "real-time" in the context of RTOS. • What are the different types of real-time systems
• How does an RTOS manage and schedule tasks or processes to • meet specific timing constraints and deadlines
• What is the role of the kernel in an RTOS, and how does it differ • from the kernel in a general-purpose OS
• Explain the significance of real-time operating systems in critical • applications, such as aviation, automotive, and industrial • control.
Compare and contrast the key differences between a generalpurpose operating system (OS) and an RTOS.
What are the strengths and limitations of using a generalpurpose OS in real-time applications versus an RTOS?
how task scheduling and resource management differ in an RTOS compared to a traditional OS
• Describe the various task scheduling methods employed in • RTOS programming, including preemptive scheduling and • cooperative scheduling.
• How does round-robin scheduling work in the context of an • RTOS? What are the advantages and limitations of this • approach
• Provide an example of a scenario where a priority-based • scheduling policy is crucial in an RTOS application.

modules.module_title: MSME/AET/03 Digital Logic design and Programming on FPGA and CPLD

pcs.pc_description: • Explain the basic architecture of a CPLD (Complex • Programmable Logic Device) and an FPGA (Field- Programmable • Gate Array). What differentiates these two devices
• Using Xilinx ISE (Integrated Software Environment), describe the • steps involved in creating a simple project for a CPLD or FPGA
• Develop a VHDL program for a full adder circuit and explain the • key components of the code.
• Explain the concept of memory blocks in system architecture. • How do these blocks store and retrieve data
• Provide an overview of the different types of interfaces found in • embedded systems, such as UART, SPI, I2C, and GPIO.
• How do domain-specific languages (DSLs) differ from generalpurpose languages? Provide examples of DSLs and their use • cases
• VHDL code snippet for a simple digital circuit, such as a 2-to-1 • multiplexer.
• How do you read and interpret HDL or VHDL code for a specific • digital design? Describe the syntax and structure of such code
• How do these tools facilitate various stages of the design • process, from conceptualization to final verification?

modules.module_title: MSME/AET/02 IoT application development on R-Pi and NodeMCU

pcs.pc_description: • What is the Internet of Things (IoT), and how does it extend the • capabilities of connected devices
• The basic concepts of programming and how Python fits into • the realm of computer programming
• The different methods of decision-making in Python, including if • statements and switch/case constructs
• Loops like for and while work in Python, and what are their use • cases
• The Python environment, including the interpreter and how it • executes Python code
• The concept of looping structures in Python and how they • enable repetitive tasks
• The use and characteristics of data structures like lists, tuples, • sets, and dictionaries in Python.
• The concept of file handling in Python, including, appending, • reading and writing to files
Provide code examples demonstrating the use of constructors and destructors.
• Concept of GPIO (General Purpose Input/output) pins and how • they can be used to interface with external devices for program • execution
• Concept of GPIO (General Purpose Input/output) pins and how • they can be used to interface with external devices for program • execution
• Example of using port programming to toggle an LED connected • to a GPIO pin
• Process of programming the Raspberry Pi to control an LED, • LCD, sensors, Actuators etc
• Adding a Bluetooth functionality to a Raspberry Pi, and what • types of Bluetooth modules are commonly used
• Explain the core components of an IoT system, including • sensors, communication protocols, and data processing
• What factors should be considered when choosing an IoT • platform for a specific project
• Example of using the ThingSpeak API to collect and analyze • sensor data from an IoT device.
The concept of interfacing IoT devices, like Arduino, with cloudbased web services and databases
• What is NodeMCU, and how does it differ from other IoT • development platforms like Arduino
• How can various sensors, such as temperature, humidity, • motion, ultrasonic, infrared, current, sound, and gas sensors, be • interfaced with an Arduino board for IoT applications
• How are actuators like relay switches, motors interfaced and • controlled using an Arduino board
